en.headline: Major banks keep prime rates unchanged after HKMA holds base rate
en.dek: HSBC, Bank of China Hong Kong and Standard Chartered maintained their best lending rates at current levels following the Monetary Authority’s decision to hold its base rate at 4.25 per cent.
body: Hong Kong’s three note-issuing banks kept their prime rates unchanged on Thursday after the Hong Kong Monetary Authority held its base rate at 4.25 per cent, matching the US Federal Reserve’s decision to keep its target range steady.

HSBC and Bank of China (Hong Kong) maintained their best lending rates at 5 per cent, while Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) kept its rate at 5.25 per cent. Savings deposit rates at the banks also remained unchanged.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority warned of considerable uncertainty over the path of US interest rates, which depend on inflation, labour market and other economic data, and noted that this could influence Hong Kong’s interest rate environment.

Local mortgage intermediaries said the city’s banking system remained liquid and interbank rates stayed relatively low, so banks faced little immediate pressure to raise prime rates even if the Federal Reserve were to tighten further later in the year.

zh.headline: 主要銀行維持最優惠利率不變 跟隨金管局按兵不動
zh.dek: 滙豐、中銀香港及渣打在金管局維持基本利率於4.25厘後，分別保持最優惠利率於5厘及5.25厘。
body: 本港三間發鈔行周四維持最優惠利率不變，此前香港金融管理局維持基本利率於4.25厘，與美國聯儲局維持目標區間不變的決定一致。
滙豐銀行及中銀香港維持最優惠利率於5厘，渣打香港則維持於5.25厘。各行港元儲蓄存款利率亦維持不變。
金管局表示，美國利率走勢仍存相當不確定性，將取決於通脹、勞工市場及其他經濟數據的發展，並可能影響香港的利率環境。
本地按揭中介指，本港銀行體系資金仍然充裕，同業拆息維持較低水平，即使聯儲局年內進一步收緊，銀行短期內上調最優惠利率的壓力亦有限。
